Article Title: 'Dismantle terror infrastructure first': India's US envoy hits out at Pakistan over Indus Waters Treaty
Article Text:

India’s envoy to the US, Vinay Mohan Kwatra said Pakistan had eroded the foundation of the Indus Waters Treaty over the past five decades. He added that Islamabad had “dismantled” the goodwill and friendship that underpinned the 1960 agreement, and that New Delhi’s decision to keep the treaty in abeyance merely acknowledged that reality.As reported by US' Newsweek magazine, Kwatra said the treaty’s preamble reflected a commitment made 'in a spirit of goodwill and friendship', but Pakistan’s conduct had weakened that foundation over half a century.“It is worth remembering that the treaty's preamble declares it was concluded ‘in a spirit of goodwill and friendship’. Pakistan spent half a century dismantling that goodwill and friendship. The abeyance merely acknowledges what Pakistan's conduct had already destroyed,” Kwatra said.His remarks came after Pakistan recently hosted a conference protesting India’s decision to keep the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) in abeyance on April 23 last year, a day after Pakistan-trained terrorists killed 26 people in Pahalgam, Jammu and Kashmir.The IWT, signed by India and Pakistan in 1960, divided the waters of the six rivers of the Indus basin between the two countries. India was given control over the eastern rivers, Ravi, Beas and Sutlej which account for about 20 per cent of the basin’s water, while Pakistan received rights over the western rivers Indus, Jhelum and Chenab carrying around 80 per cent.“That asymmetry stifled development for decades in Indian regions that could have benefited from better water rights. India honoured the treaty anyway,” Kwatra said according to Newsweek.The envoy said Pakistan’s approach towards India had been marked by wars, hostility and cross-border terrorism, citing the 1965, 1971 and 1999 conflicts along with major terror attacks, including the 2001 Parliament attack, the 2008 Mumbai attacks, the 2016 Uri and Pathankot attacks, the 2019 Pulwama attack and the 2025 Pahalgam attack.Kwatra also said that if Pakistan sincerely wanted India’s cooperation on bilateral issues, it must first dismantle the terror infrastructure it has built over the years.On implementation of the treaty, Kwatra alleged that Pakistan had repeatedly delayed Indian projects and opposed efforts to revisit the agreement in view of changing technology and requirements.“Pakistan also consistently blocked India's initiatives to renegotiate the treaty in light of six decades of technological change, which would have let India develop its hydropower potential,” Kwatra added.“Bit by bit, Pakistan eroded India's faith that it could exercise its rights under the treaty, or hope for a better one suited to today's realities,” he said.Responding to calls for India and Pakistan to resume talks, Kwatra said past initiatives had failed to address core concerns.“Prime Minister Narendra Modi has clearly voiced India’s stand today: ‘Terror and talks cannot go together... Terror and trade cannot go together... Water and blood cannot flow together',” Kwatra said.Kwatra also said Pakistan should focus on improving its own water management instead of blaming India for its challenges."The Government of Pakistan would do better to fix its dismal water productivity, than to stage conferences blaming India and issuing threats,” he said, adding, “The habit of pinning every domestic failure on India has grown old."
Article Summary: India’s envoy to the us, vinay mohan kwatra said pakistan had eroded the foundation of the indus waters treaty over the past five decades. He added that islamabad had “dismantled” the goodwill and friendship that underpinned the 1960 agreement. The iwt, signed by india and pakistan in 1960, divided the waters of the six rivers of theindus basin between the countries.

Whether it is creating fast-track mechanisms or incorporating suggestions from the states, we are working in that direction."The Prime Minister said paper leaks had affected governments across the country for decades and jeopardised the future of students.PM Modi reiterated that the government would act firmly against those involved in paper leak rackets.

NEW DELHI: A day after resigning from the party, former BJP national spokesperson Shehzad Poonawalla on Saturday released an Instagram video saying he was “disappointed” with Prime Minister Narendra Modi In a sarcastic jibe at the Congress and its most prominent face, leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi , Poonawalla said that unlike Congress prime ministers, PM Modi, despite being in office for 12 years, was still to become a “dictator."Poonawalla’s remarks came after PM Modi, in his fifth Instagram video since the recent student protests in Delhi, said he had “forgiven” protesters who allegedly abused him and his late mother during the agitation. Several people, mostly youngsters, were booked for allegedly abusing the PM and his mother, after the protests ended with the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan as Union education minister on July 25.“I am completely disappointed with Prime Minister Narendra Modi. It has been 12 years and he has still not learnt how to be a dictator,” Poonawalla said in his Hindi video, adding that instead of becoming a dictator, the prime minister appealed for those who abused him to be forgiven.He urged the prime minister to learn “real dictatorship” from former prime ministers Indira Gandhi and Jawaharlal Nehru, Rahul Gandhi’s grandmother and great-grandfather, respectively. Poonawalla, a former Congress member, also referred to cases filed against students in Congress-ruled Karnataka and Kerala.He further referred to the alleged curbing of free speech during Nehru’s tenure and invoked the Emergency imposed by Indira Gandhi in 1975.“Who got all parliamentarians put in jail? Indira Gandhi. Who ordered police to fire at seers? Indira Gandhi,” Poonawalla remarked.The second incident he referred to appeared to be a reference to the 1966 police firing on protesters outside Parliament during a demonstration demanding a nationwide ban on cow slaughter.The former BJP spokesperson also referred to several protest movements that he alleged were “crushed” by Congress governments at the Centre and in various states.“We saw during the 2011 Anna Hazare agitation that 1,200-1,300 people were arrested. Anna Hazare himself was arrested. Rajbala lost her life,” he remarked, referring to the anti-corruption movement led by activist Anna Hazare that had put the then Congress-led UPA government under pressure.Rajbala was a woman protester who died following a Delhi Police crackdown at Ramlila Ground during the agitation.“Come on, Modi ji. It has been 12 years and you have still not become a dictator. You have poured water on the hopes of the Left-liberals,” Poonawalla concluded.PM Modi’s Instagram videos have been described as an attempt by the prime minister to reach out to “Gen Z” — the demographic with the largest participation in the recent student protests.

He says pm modi, despite being in office for 12 years, was still to become a 'dictator' his remarks came after pm modi said he had 'forgiven' protesters who abused him and his mother.

Article Title: Judge Ujjal Bhuyan questions SC collegium’s opacity
Article Text:
Citizens have right to know deliberations on elevation, transfer of judges: Bhuyan

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: SC judge Ujjal Bhuyan has questioned opacity in the collegium’s decisions on judicial appointments.“I have noticed that the last three collegium resolutions contain no reasons whatsoever. Is this a step back from the principle of transparency?” said Justice Bhuyan at a panel discussion on Saturday. “By withholding reasons, we also create space for individuals to enter the judiciary who may later describe groups of people as ‘ants’ and make other remarks that are wholly unconstitutional,” he said.To prevent the entry of such people, “there should be some discussion, there should be some reasons given”, said Justice Ujjal Bhuyan. Though the judge didn’t name anyone, the comment was an apparent reference to a remark by an Allahabad high court judge at a social event in 2024.He was speaking at the launch of the Judicial Transparency Index: Assessing Disclosure of Information by the Supreme Court and the High Courts, prepared by the Justice, Access and Lowering Delays in India (JALDI) Initiative at the Vidhi Centre for Legal Policy.The judge stressed that deliberations on the elevation and transfer of judges by the SC collegium largely remain confidential, contrary to the principle of judicial transparency.“While carrying out the next assessment on the scale of Judicial Transparency Index, I may request the JALDI team to also look into the aspect of opacity of the collegium system. Deliberations on elevation and transfer of judges remain confidential. Reasons for rejecting or deferring a recommendation are rarely disclosed in full. And the criteria applied are not codified in any publicly disclosed instrument. It is a very important issue. Citizens have a right to know what is happening in the courts. They have a right to know who would be their judges.They have a right to know judgments. These should be in the public domain”, Justice Bhuyan underlined.The report is the first systematic study assessing transparency practices across India’s higher judiciary and evaluates disclosure of information by the Supreme Court and high courts across judicial processes, institutional governance and administration, and judicial and administrative personnel.Referring to a previous collegium resolution reiterating the recommendation of senior advocate Saurabh Kirpal for appointment as a judge, Justice Bhuyan said he found the reasons recorded by the Supreme Court convincing but noted that despite more than three and a half years having passed, no appointment materialised.Key findings of the JALDI report reveal that only five high courts have published a budget on their websites for FY 2025-26 while none has published the criteria governing case allocation.Of the 813 judges in the higher judiciary, only 87 have publicly disclosed their assets even as only two high courts publish disciplinary sanction orders pertaining to district judicial officers.“The findings highlight that the level of judicial transparency varies across courts and demonstrate that while individual disclosure measures have emerged...they have not yet translated into a holistic approach...” a release from Vidhi said.
Article Summary: Citizens have right to know deliberations on elevation, transfer of judges: bhuyan. Only five high courts have published a budget on their websites for fy 2025-26 while none has published the criteria governing case allocation. Of the 813 judges in the higher judiciary, only 87 have publicly disclosed their assets.

Article Title: ‘My return to Kolkata proves injustice cannot be permanent’: Taslima Nasreen
Article Text:
Exiled Bangladeshi author Taslima Nasreen in Kolkata. (PTI Photo)

NEW DELHI: Exiled Bangladeshi author Taslima Nasreen on Saturday described her return to India after nearly two decades as proof that “injustice can be long but cannot be permanent. ”She made the remarks at an event in Kolkata, nearly two decades after she was forced to leave the city in 2007. The 63-year-old writer had been living in Kolkata since leaving Bangladesh in 1994 amid alleged death threats from radical groups over her writings and views on religion.Nasreen, who has been living in Europe since leaving Kolkata, also clarified that her return to the city was not linked to any "political agenda.""Today, the opening of this door proves that injustice can be long, but it cannot be permanent. History remembers who closed the doors and who opened them...I am not here to speak for any political party, or against any party. I am here to speak in favour of women's rights," PTI quoted her as saying.She also expressed concern over what she described as a "rise" in religious extremism in Bangladesh."I am against all forms of fundamentalism, but I have spoken against Islamic fundamentalists because I have seen it from close quarters since childhood.The rise of fundamentalism in Bangladesh is at an alarming stage. Freedom of speech is being curtailed," Nasreen said.Visibly emotional, Nasreen called her return a "fulfilment of a long-awaited moment.""It took me 19 years to say these words: 'I have returned to Kolkata.' I felt the pain of losing an address every single day. On August 8, 1994, the then government forced me to leave Bangladesh. The state may have removed me from my country, but it could never remove my country from within me," she added.Lamenting that she could not find a permanent home in either Bangladesh or West Bengal, Nasreen highlighted that Europe had provided her security but not a sense of belonging."Europe has given me citizenship and a place to live, but unfortunately, I couldn't get a small place to stay in the two Bengals. Europe gave me security, but it could not give me a sense of belonging. A home is not built by security alone; it is built by language, memory and culture," Nasreen remarked.Nasreen maintained that she had never been convicted by any court but had faced restrictions because of opposition from fundamentalist groups."I committed no crime. No court has ever punished me. It is a painful truth of our times that a writer needs police protection to visit the city of her own language."Rejecting allegations that her writings were offensive, she emphasised that her advocacy had focused on equality and human rights."I only spoke about equal rights for women and men, and about human rights irrespective of religion or caste. I said that any rule or doctrine that takes away equality and human dignity must be changed."She also criticised what she described as the unequal treatment of women in the name of religion and backed a Uniform Civil Code across South Asia, arguing that religion-based personal laws discriminate against women."The real conflict is between secularism and fundamentalism, between the rational mind and irrationality, between innovation and tradition, and between people who value freedom and those who do not."
Article Summary: Taslima nasreen was forced to leave kolkata in 1994 amid alleged death threats. The 63-year-old writer had been living in europe since leaving the city in 2007. Nasreen said her return to india was not linked to any "political agenda"

Article Title: Nathula pass border trade resumes after 6 years; traders seek expansion of goods list
Article Text:
Nathula Border gate (ANI image)

Traders seek expansion of trade list

Around 300 traders await passes

Border trade through the Nathula Pass in East Sikkim, a key segment of the ancient Silk Route connecting India and China, resumed on Saturday after remaining suspended for nearly six years. A formal reopening ceremony was held at Nathula, with officials from both countries participating in the event.The trade route had remained closed since 2020 due to the Covid-19 pandemic and subsequent border tensions between India and China.Welcoming the resumption of trade, Anil Gupta, General Secretary of the Indo-China Nathula Border Traders Welfare Association, thanked Sikkim Chief Minister Prem Singh Tamang for his efforts in facilitating the reopening."I extend heartfelt thanks to our Chief Minister, Prem Singh Tamang. This has become possible today solely due to his efforts. For traders who had outstanding dues or stocks stranded on the other side, this is a time of great joy, and everyone is happy," Gupta said.While welcoming the resumption of trade, Gupta said the existing list of goods permitted through Nathula needs to be updated to reflect present-day commercial needs."The current trading list includes items like horses, sheep and general goods. We believe industrial products relevant to today's times should be included. We have submitted a formal request to the department, and we are hopeful that the government will take a very positive view of this," he said.Under the existing arrangement, only a limited list of traditional goods is allowed to be traded through the border route. Traders have long been seeking the inclusion of industrial and other commercially relevant products.Gupta said preparations for the resumption of trade were underway, with authorities verifying applications submitted by traders."Around five hundred traders collected forms, and approximately three hundred have submitted them. Verification is underway, and we hope all traders will receive their passes very soon," he said.The reopening is expected to revive economic activity in the border region and provide relief to traders whose businesses had been affected by the prolonged suspension of cross-border trade. Nathula, located in East Sikkim, is one of the few officially designated border trading points between India and China and has historically served as an important corridor on the ancient Silk Route.
Article Summary: Nathula pass in east sikkim, a key segment of the ancient silk route connecting india and china, resumed trade on saturday. The trade route had remained closed since 2020 due to the covid-19 pandemic and subsequent border tensions. Traders have long been seeking the inclusion of industrial and other commercially relevant products.

Article Title: 'In every national security decision, Doval had a role': Amit Shah praises NSA at award ceremony
Article Text:

'First selection' after Modi became PM

NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Saturday lauded National Security Advisor (NSA) Ajit Doval for his contribution to India's national security and foreign policy, saying the veteran intelligence officer has played a crucial role behind every major national security decision taken by Prime Minister Narendra Modi since 2014.Speaking at a function in Pune after presenting the Lokmanya Tilak National Award 2026 to Doval, Shah said the NSA's advice and strategic inputs have been instrumental in strengthening India's security architecture and defence preparedness.He also said Doval's contribution to India's internal and external security had been so significant that history would reserve "a golden page" for him."NSA Ajit Doval has played a great role in strengthening India's foreign policy. In every decision of PM Modi for national security, Doval has had a 'role and advice' in the background," Shah said."Whenever history is written, if anyone analyses internal security and external security, then clearly, for Ajit Doval ji, a golden page will have to be kept reserved; there is no doubt about this," he added.Shah said one of the first decisions taken by PM Modi after assuming office in 2014 was appointing Doval as the National Security Advisor, a move he said transformed India's strategic posture."Today, India's foreign policy has become a foreign policy with a backbone of steel; no one can deny this. We have, along with self-respect, strengthened our position in the world," Shah said.Praising Doval's decades-long career in the Intelligence Bureau, Shah said India has emerged as a stronger and more confident nation under Modi's leadership, with Doval making a significant contribution to that transformation."After becoming NSA in 2014, Doval helped implement many strategic ideas on the ground and played a major role in modernising India's armed forces, strengthening technology, enhancing operational capability and improving the country's defence preparedness," Shah said.He added that the Modi government has fundamentally transformed both the defensive and offensive capabilities of the armed forces over the past 12 years, with Doval playing a key role in the process.Shah also noted that much of Doval's contribution can never be made public because of the confidential nature of intelligence operations.Recalling his tenure as Gujarat's home minister, Shah narrated how he first interacted with Doval following the Ahmedabad serial bomb blasts. He said then chief minister Narendra Modi had advised Gujarat Police to consult Doval while investigating the attacks."I remember Ajit ji had come to my house. The tips he gave resulted in Gujarat Police resolving not just the Ahmedabad bomb blast, but 13 bomb blasts across the country all at once. This was a very great achievement," Shah said.The Union home minister also paid tribute to Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak, calling him one of the foremost architects of India's freedom movement.He said Tilak's iconic slogan, "Swarajya is my birthright, and I shall have it," gave a new direction to India's freedom struggle and inspired generations of freedom fighters.Shah added that the slogan made Indians realise that self-rule was their right and not a favour bestowed by anyone.Describing Tilak as a fearless journalist, Shah said one could truly understand courage in journalism only by reading the articles published in Kesari, the newspaper founded by the freedom fighter."How fearless a journalist can be can only be experienced by reading the articles of Kesari," he said.Referring to Tilak's role in mobilising people through the public Ganesh and Shivaji festivals, Shah said they laid the foundation for cultural nationalism and that India continues to follow the path envisioned by the freedom fighter."India is now moving firmly on the path of cultural nationalism laid down by Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak, and no one can reverse that journey," he said.Shah further added that Tilak's ideas on nationalism, self-rule and social awakening continue to guide the country and remain relevant for nation-building, particularly for the younger generation.Shah said honours such as the Lokmanya Tilak National Award are not merely ceremonial but recognise those who dedicate their lives to the country and inspire future generations."When such individuals are honoured, the feeling of gratitude of society towards them is discharged... Today, the Tilak Award that has been conferred upon Ajit Doval ji... for those who live for this country and work for this country, it will become a place of great inspiration," he said.Accepting the Lokmanya Tilak National Award, Doval thanked the organisers and said he was honoured to receive an award named after Lokmanya Tilak."I am thankful for this award named after Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak and accept it with humility," Doval said.Doval also praised the country's leadership, saying, "We are very fortunate to have leaders like PM Modi and Amit Shah".
Article Summary: Amit shah presented lokmanya tilak award to ajit doval and hailed his role in india's national security. Shah said the nsa's advice and strategic inputs have been instrumental in strengthening india's security architecture and defence preparedness.

Article Title: President Murmu assents to anti-paper leak amendment Bill
Article Text:
President Droupadi Murmu has given assent to the Bill

NEW DELHI: President Droupadi Murmu has given assent to the Bill amending the anti-paper leak law, days after Parliament passed the legislation to introduce stricter penalties for examination-related malpractices.In a Gazette notification issued on Friday, the ministry of law and justice said the President has given assent to the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, days after it was passed by both Houses of Parliament earlier this week.The Centre said the amendments highlight its commitment to strengthening the integrity of public examinations and safeguarding the interests of students.The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026 was passed by the Rajya Sabha through a voice vote on Thursday amid a walkout by several Opposition parties belonging to the INDIA bloc. The Lok Sabha had cleared the legislation a day earlier.Soon after Parliament passed the Bill, Prime Minister Narendra Modi shared a video message on Instagram, saying that the "important task of making a stringent law against paper leaks has been completed."The Prime Minister said the government was taking steps to curb paper leaks and examination malpractices, adding that it had become imperative to strengthen the examination system through the use of the latest technology. He also said the government was working to ensure that "no paper-leak mafia plays with the future of students."Under the amended law, individuals found guilty of paper leaks or using unfair means in public examinations will face imprisonment ranging from five to 10 years, along with a fine of up to Rs 50 lakh.For organised offences, the legislation prescribes a minimum jail term of seven years and a fine of not less than Rs 10 crore.
Article Summary: President droupadi murmu has given assent to the bill amending the anti-paper leak law. Parliament passed the legislation to introduce stricter penalties for examination-related malpractices. Prime minister narendra modi shared a video message on instagram, saying that the "important task of making a stringent law against paper leaks has been completed"

Article Title: NSA Ajit Doval receives Lokmanya Tilak National Award for national security contribution
Article Text:
Ajit Doval is the country's longest-serving National Security Advisor.

NEW DELHI: National Security Advisor (NSA) Ajit Doval on Saturday received the Lokmanya Tilak National Award in Pune in recognition of his contribution to strengthening India's national security.Union home minister Amit Shah presented the award at a ceremony held on the 106th death anniversary of freedom fighter Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak.The event took place at the Kataria High School ground in Mukundnagar and was attended by Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis, deputy chief ministers Eknath Shinde and Sunetra Pawar, along with several senior political leaders and dignitaries.The award, presented by the Lokmanya Tilak Smarak Trust, honours individuals for their outstanding contribution to the nation. Trust president Rohit Tilak had earlier announced that Doval was chosen this year for his role in strengthening India's national security.Doval, the country's longest-serving National Security Advisor, has played a key role in shaping India's security strategy and has been associated with several major operations, including Operation Sindoor, the Balakot air strike and the surgical strikes .Instituted in 1983, the Lokmanya Tilak National Award has previously been conferred on several eminent personalities. Veteran socialist S M Joshi was the first recipient of the honour. Former President Pranab Mukherjee, Prime Ministers Narendra Modi, Atal Bihari Vajpayee and Manmohan Singh are among the distinguished recipients. Union minister Nitin Gadkari received the award last year.
Article Summary: Ajit doval is the country's longest-serving national security advisor. He has played a key role in shaping india's security strategy. Doval has been associated with several major operations, including operation sindoor and the balakot air strike. The lokmanya tilak national award has previously been conferred on several eminent personalities.

Because of this, the future of our children has also been put at risk," he said.The Prime Minister added that the government had recognised the need for reforms in the education system and greater use of technology to safeguard the integrity of examinations.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Sigmund Freud: 'The more perfect a person is on the outside, the more demons they have on the inside' and why absolute perfection is a facade
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Sigmund Freud

Appearance vs reality

Absolute perfection is a cover-up

Psychological repression

Sigmund Freud was an Austrian neurologist who lived from 1856 to 1939. He is best known as the founding father of psychoanalysis, a clinical method for treating mental health conditions through dialogue between a patient and a psychoanalyst. Freud revolutionized how humanity views the mind by suggesting that much of human behavior is driven by thoughts, desires, and memories locked away in the unconscious mind. Before Freud, mental health was largely viewed through biological or religious lenses. Freud introduced the idea that our internal conflicts, hidden desires, and childhood experiences heavily shape who we are as adults.Most of his quotes entered the academic realm of psychology study and one of them is an observation about appearance and reality. "The more perfect a person is on the outside, the more demons they have on the inside," Freud said.The idea behind the statement that a person who appears perfect on the outside hides demons on the inside ties directly into Freud's theories about how the human mind manages forbidden urges and societal expectations. Freud divided the human psyche into three main parts: the id, the ego, and the superego. The id is the primitive part of our mind that operates purely on instinct, pleasure, and selfish desires.The superego is the exact opposite. It represents our moral conscience, internalized societal rules, ideals, and perfectionism. The ego sits in the middle, trying to balance the wild desires of the id with the strict, moral demands of the superego.When a person tries to project an image of absolute perfection to the world, their superego is working in overdrive. Society rewards people who are polite, composed, highly successful, and morally spotless. To maintain this flawless exterior, a person must constantly suppress any thoughts, feelings, or impulses that society might judge negatively. These suppressed thoughts do not simply vanish. Instead, Freud argued that they get pushed down into the unconscious mind. In this context, the demons refer to these repressed instincts, hidden anger, sexual urges, envy, and unresolved traumas that the person refuses to acknowledge publicly or even to themselves.The core mechanism at work here is psychological repression. Freud believed that repression takes an enormous amount of mental energy. The more energy a person spends trying to look perfect, pristine, and composed, the more pressure builds up inside their unconscious mind. Imagine pushing an inflatable beach ball under the water. The deeper you push it down, and the longer you hold it there, the more force it exerts back against your hands. The surface of the water may look smooth and still, but under the surface, a huge amount of pressure is building up. The demons are not literal evil spirits, but rather those submerged feelings that are desperate to burst back up to the surface.Extreme perfectionism often serves as a defense mechanism. Freud identified several defense mechanisms that the mind uses to protect itself from anxiety. One of these is called reaction formation. Reaction formation happens when a person feels an urge that they consider unacceptable, so they unconsciously act in the exact opposite way to hide it. For instance, someone who struggles with strong feelings of internal chaos, aggression, or self-doubt might overcompensate by becoming obsessed with neatness, strict control, and outward moral purity. The shiny, spotless exterior is actually a protective shield designed to hide the internal turmoil that the person is deeply afraid of facing.This concept also explains why hyper-perfect facades can eventually break down dramatically. Because maintaining a flawless persona requires constant vigilance, the mind eventually tires. When the ego becomes exhausted, the repressed material in the unconscious mind finds sneaky ways to escape. This can show up as sudden emotional outbursts, physical illnesses with no clear medical cause, severe anxiety, or self-destructive behavior that seems to come out of nowhere to outside observers. To the public, it looks like a sudden fall from grace, but from a psychoanalytic perspective, it is simply the long-contained internal pressure finally bursting through the seams of a rigid outward image.Freud’s insight reminds us that genuine human health is not about achieving flawless perfection, but about achieving self-awareness and balance. When people try to disown their darker, flawed, or messy emotions to appear perfect to others, those emotions do not disappear. They grow stronger in the dark corners of the mind. Accepting that human nature is naturally flawed allows people to integrate their shadow side rather than fight it. A person who can acknowledge their weaknesses, mistakes, and complicated feelings does not need to build a fake wall of perfection, and as a result, they carry far fewer hidden demons inside.
Article Summary: Sigmund freud was an austrian neurologist who lived from 1856 to 1939. He is best known as the founding father of psychoanalysis. Freud revolutionized how humanity views the mind by suggesting that much of human behavior is driven by thoughts, desires, and memories locked away in the unconscious mind.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Mohammed bin Salman: 'I fear that the day I die, I am going to die without accomplishing what I have in my mind'
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Mohammed bin Salman.

"Because I fear that the day I die, I am going to die without accomplishing what I have in my mind. Life is too short, and a lot of things can happen, and I am really keen to see it with my own eyes, and that is why I am in a hurry."

MBS and a radical departure from traditional Saudi leadership

Philosophy behind the quote

In November 2017, New York Times foreign affairs columnist Thomas L Friedman conducted a landmark interview with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman in Riyadh. During their conversation, Friedman observed the relentless, around-the-clock work culture among the young prince and his senior advisers. Friedman noted that MBS's intense work habits reminded him of a famous line from the musical Hamilton, in which the chorus asks why the protagonist always works like he is "running out of time".When asked directly why he operated at such a breakneck pace, Mohammed bin Salman offered his candid response:Mohammed bin Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, widely known as MBS, serves as the Crown Prince and Prime Minister of Saudi Arabia . Born in 1985, his rise within the Saudi governance structure was swift. When his father, King Salman bin Abdulaziz, ascended the throne in early 2015, MBS was appointed Minister of Defense. Soon after, he took control of the Council of Economic and Development Affairs (CEDA), giving him direction over the kingdom's economic policy, sovereign wealth fund, and domestic security apparatus.In June 2017, he was formally elevated to Crown Prince.MBS represented a radical departure from traditional Saudi leadership. For decades, the kingdom was led by older monarchs who favored slow, consensus-based, and deeply conservative governance. In contrast, MBS established a centralized, top-down leadership style designed to push rapid economic and cultural changes across the country.While MBS expressed his personal goal and feelings, the quote is a reminder of mortality and human fear of running out of time before what they think needs to be done.When someone says they are in a hurry because life is short and they want to see their ideas become reality, they are dealing with a few basic ideas.First, it is about facing the reality that we all die. Most people try not to think about death, but focusing on the fact that time is limited can act like a wake-up call. It creates a powerful urge to stop waiting around and get things done immediately. The biggest fear here is not death itself, but dying with your work unfinished and your ideas left trapped in your head.Second, it shows a deep desire to turn an inner vision into real-life results. Everyone has ideas, but some people feel an intense personal responsibility to build those ideas into the physical world. They treat life like a race against the clock to prove that their thoughts were not just empty dreams, but something real.Third, it is about wanting to see the results yourself. A lot of people build things for the far future, accepting that they won't be around to see the final product. But this quote pushes back against that idea. It comes from a wish to be alive to witness the change firsthand, rather than leaving it for future generations to enjoy.Finally, it reflects a belief that one person's energy can speed up the world. Instead of letting changes happen slowly over decades, it is the mindset that if you work hard enough and push fast enough, you can force the future to arrive much sooner.
Article Summary: Mohammed bin salman bin abdulaziz al saud, widely known as mbs, serves as the crown prince and prime minister of saudi arabia. Mbs represented a radical departure from traditional saudi leadership. The quote is a reminder of mortality and human fear of running out of time before what they think needs to be done.

Article Title: Erica Fox cause of death revealed as new autopsy sheds light on triathlete's final moments
Article Text:
Erica Fox (Image Via Getty)

Erica Fox autopsy reveals how one shark bite turned fatal

The Mercury News

Erica Fox was an experienced triathlete who understood the risks

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Erica Fox, a 55-year-old triathlete and experienced open-water swimmer, died after a single shark bite caused devastating injuries during a group swim in California’s Monterey Bay on December 21, 2025. A newly released autopsy found the bite shattered her pelvis, severed a major artery and left her underwater, leading to her drowning. The findings have now revealed how the tragic attack unfolded and why she could not survive.Erica Fox, a 55-year-old triathlete and experienced open-water swimmer, died after a single shark bite caused devastating injuries during a group swim in California’s Monterey Bay on December 21, 2025. A newly released autopsy found that the bite fractured her pelvis, severed a major artery and left her underwater, where she drowned. The findings have now given a clearer picture of the tragic attack that shocked the local swimming community.According to the autopsy, Fox died from drowning along with sharp and blunt-force injuries caused by the shark attack. The report said one extremely powerful bite stretched from her right knee to her abdomen.Her pelvis was broken in several places, and a major artery was cut. Investigators also found serious injuries to her right knee, thigh and abdomen, while her wetsuit was torn in the same areas as the wounds.Fox disappeared while swimming with the Kelp Krawlers, an open-water swimming group she helped start. The group was heading toward Lovers Point Beach, and she was swimming ahead of most of the others when she suddenly vanished.Around the same time, a driver called 911 after seeing a shark leap out of the water about 100 yards off Lovers Point. The witness told authorities it looked like a person was in the shark’s mouth before the animal disappeared beneath the surface. As swimmers rushed back to shore and counted everyone, they realized Fox was missing.Her husband of 30 years, Jean-Francois Vanreusel, was also part of the swim that day. Sharon Carey, who stayed closer to shore during the swim, later told, “It started to click that everybody was back on shore but Erica. I just felt numb. I was hoping that maybe she got out of the water and then decided to walk back.”Emergency crews launched a massive search using boats, helicopters and divers. After nearly 15 hours, the official search was called off, but the Monterey County Sheriff’s Office continued working with Bedrock Ocean Exploration and the Angel’s Recovery Dive Team. Fox’s body was found six days later after washing ashore near Wilder Ranch State Park.Friends said Fox loved the ocean and never stayed away from a challenge. She had completed two Half-Ironman races and took part in the Escape from Alcatraz triathlon for nearly 20 years, according to her father, who spoke with NBC News.She had also attended a “Sharktober” seminar at Hopkins Marine Station to learn more about sharks and ocean safety.Lisa Jensen, a fellow Kelp Krawlers member, remembered Fox as “an incredibly cheerful, bubbly, funny, joyful, kind human being” who understood the risks that came with open-water swimming.Her death was the third shark attack linked to Lovers Point since June 2022. Another Kelp Krawlers member, Steve Bruemmer, survived a serious shark attack in the same area in 2022.While shark attacks remain rare along the California coast, Fox’s death has renewed attention on the dangers that can exist even for experienced swimmers.
Article Summary: Erica fox, 55, died after a single shark bite caused devastating injuries during a group swim in california’s monterey bay on december 21, 2025. A newly released autopsy found the bite shattered her pelvis, severed a major artery and left her underwater, leading to her drowning.

Article Title: US, Israel weigh bombarding Iran's energy infrastructure through the weekend: Report
Article Text:
US, Israel eye weekend bombing campaign on Iran's energy sites

The United States and Israel are planning a potential bombing campaign targeting Iran's energy infrastructure, with strikes possibly taking place over the weekend, CBS News reported on Friday, citing sources.However, US president Donald Trump has not yet given final approval for the operation.According to multiple US sources, officials have discussed wrapping up the operation before financial markets open on Monday amid concerns over the potential impact of the strikes on the US and global economy.However, no firm timeline has been finalised.The sources added that Israeli officials have been informed of the plans and are coordinating closely with the United States.A joint operation would mark Israel's return to active military operations after it paused its campaign during the US-brokered truce.Iran, meanwhile, has not launched attacks against Israel since the memorandum of understanding collapsed and the United States resumed combat operations in early July."Israel is unaware of a decision to restart full military operations, nor has been requested of Israel to join any military actions against Iran," an Israeli official was quoted as saying by CBS News.The development comes as Trump warned on Friday that Iran could be hit "very hard.""We'll be hitting him very hard and, you know, at some point they're going to say, 'We just can't take it anymore'," the US president said.The Wall Street Journal also reported that Trump had ordered preparations for a fresh military offensive aimed at pressuring Tehran into surrender, with the operation potentially beginning as early as this weekend.More than five months after the conflict began on February 28, when the United States and Israel launched strikes on Iran, the fighting shows no sign of easing, with both sides continuing to exchange attacks.Throughout the conflict, Trump has repeatedly threatened to target Iran's critical infrastructure. Last week, he warned that the United States would destroy a bridge or power plant each time commercial shipping in the strategically important Strait of Hormuz came under attack.The latest report also comes days after Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu met Trump and US defence secretary Pete Hegseth in Washington.
Article Summary: Us, israel eye weekend bombing campaign on iran's energy sites. Officials have discussed wrapping up the operation before financial markets open on monday. No firm timeline has been finalised, according to us sources. Israeli officials have been informed of the plans and are coordinating with the united states.

Article Title: US makes $20,000 visa bond programme permanent; India not on 50-country list
Article Text:
India not on list

Who will be affected?

The US State Department has decided to make its visa bond programme permanent after successfully running it as a pilot scheme, expanding a policy aimed at reducing visa overstays. The programme currently applies to citizens of 50 countries.Under the new rule, consular officers may require certain applicants for US visitor visas to post a bond of up to $20,000 before a visa is issued. The regulation takes effect on August 3, when it is scheduled to be published in the Federal Register. US officials have indicated that additional countries could be added to the programme in the future, Reuters cites.The visa bond programme currently covers citizens of 50 countries, including Bangladesh, Nepal and Bhutan, but India is not among them. This means Indian applicants for B-1 (business) and B-2 (tourist) visas are not affected by the new rule at present.However, the State Department has indicated that more countries could be added to the programme in the future.The rule applies to applicants seeking B-1 (business) and B-2 (tourism) visas from countries covered under the programme.According to the Federal Register notice, "Consular officers may require covered nonimmigrant visa applicants to post a bond of up to $20,000 as a condition of visa issuance, as determined by the consular officers."The State Department said a year-long review of the pilot programme found that visa bonds were effective in encouraging travellers to comply with the terms of their stay in the United States.During the pilot programme launched in 2025, consular officers could require visa applicants to post bonds of $5,000, $10,000 or $15,000.Under the permanent rule, the $5,000 option has been removed and the maximum bond amount has been increased to $20,000.Immigration and rights advocates have criticised the policy, arguing that requiring applicants to deposit thousands of dollars could discourage legitimate travel to the United States.The visa bond programme is part of a broader immigration crackdown under President Donald Trump.
Article Summary: The us state department has decided to make its visa bond programme permanent. The policy is aimed at reducing visa overstays. It currently covers citizens of 50 countries, including bangladesh, nepal and bhutan. India is not on the list of countries covered by the programme.
